description: RULEBOOK L10 blast-radius map: change type -> the doc-type prefixes that must be reviewed, plus the public-sanitisation rule that applies. Consumed by tools/docgen/adjudication.py (load_impact_map / compute_change_impact). Advisory and fail-open: an unknown change type yields a non-blocking finding naming the gap, never a block. Prefixes must exist in TAXONOMY.md. This file is locked -- it is listed in VERSION.json's rulebook_files.

DETECTOR_CHANGE.description: A rule, threshold, or classifier that decides an outcome changed. Any document stating what the system detects, or quoting a result it produced, may now be wrong.
DETECTOR_CHANGE.public_sanitization_rule: Restate the observable behaviour and its direction; never publish the threshold, weight, or cutoff that produced it (L6). Re-verify every quoted result before republishing -- a stale number under a new rule is a false claim, not an outdated one.

VISUAL_STYLE_CHANGE.description: Design tokens, typography, component styling, or theme derivation changed. Rendered output and any figure described in prose may no longer match.
VISUAL_STYLE_CHANGE.public_sanitization_rule: Re-render every affected figure and re-read the prose that describes it -- a caption describing the old visual is a defect the build cannot see. Contrast must stay above the legibility floor (L21); expressiveness never buys an exception.

USER_POLICY_CHANGE.description: What a consumer is permitted to do, see, or receive changed -- entitlements, limits, retention, or the terms of access.
USER_POLICY_CHANGE.public_sanitization_rule: Publish the rule as it now stands, with its effective date. Never describe internal enforcement mechanics or per-account overrides. A policy document that lags the enforced policy is worse than none, because it is trusted.

ARCHITECTURE_CHANGE.description: A component, boundary, or connection between parts changed -- something moved, split, merged, or was removed.
ARCHITECTURE_CHANGE.public_sanitization_rule: Publish roles and their connections, never internal hostnames, paths, or topology that maps to real infrastructure (L4). Record the decision as an ADR: an architecture change with no recorded reason becomes folklore within a quarter.

RULE_CHANGE.description: A locked rule in the rulebook itself changed. This is the highest-blast-radius change type: every document reasoning from the rule is downstream of it.
RULE_CHANGE.public_sanitization_rule: Follow L9 in full: bump VERSION.json, append the CHG entry, record the ADR, then re-baseline the rulebook hash. Re-read every document that cites the changed law by number -- an L-number reference that now points at different semantics is invisible to every mechanical check.
